featured_reviews.review_text: I had a fantastic dining experience at this restaurant. The food was absolutely delicious—every dish was full of flavor and clearly made with fresh, high-quality ingredients. From appetizers to dessert, everything was perfectly cooked and well-seasoned. The presentation was beautiful, and the portion sizes were generous. If you appreciate great taste and attention to detail in every bite, this is definitely a place worth visiting. Highly recommend!

featured_reviews.name: Nitin Malhotra
featured_reviews.review_text: Food was good. Interiors are good too. Quantity was cool. One key issue i found was the outside had a bad smell. The area was very quiet. Cooling at the Resturant could have been maintained.

featured_reviews.name: Amol M
featured_reviews.review_text:
A spacious restaurant where one can enjoy good Chinese cuisine. Serves quite a variety of dishes one can choose from. The Squid is delicious! One can have a Prawn Fried Rice along with it.
Have been there in the afternoons most of the time. Courteous service and quick to the table orders.
Found it a bit spicy but enjoyed the taste.
Servings are sumptuous and the above two dishes made a good meal for two heavy eaters. Recommend you order not more than two dishes even if you wish to try a broad variety of food.

featured_reviews.name: Vaibhav Bhosale
featured_reviews.review_text: This place is located near Sassoon dock at a walkable distance. This place was suggested by one of the friend living in that area. The food was good and staff were helpful in ordering with the food . Service too was quick and it was not a rush time. So overall nice place to visit

featured_reviews.name: jasleen wadhwa
featured_reviews.review_text: This is a cozy place ahead of sasoon dock. Amazing vibrant interiors and good ambience. Its a family place so you will be super comfy with your family there. They have a vast menu serving authentic Chinese. The servers are calm and polite. I started with soup, ordering hot and sour chicken soup and veg manchow soup which tasted great. For appetizers we had hot dragon chicken, it was nice and tasted good. For the mains burnt garlic fried rice and chicken in basil sauce was ordered which was good but tasted similar to hot dragon. They have some good beverages and desserts too. Overall i would rate it a 6/10 as for me the MSG level was a bit high in the food. Do go try this place if you are around

featured_reviews.name: Akhil Maheswaran
featured_reviews.review_text: If you are Chinese food lover then it will be the best in this area. Rather than Chinese all other food items listed in the menu also give a signature of their own taste. The best part of this restaurant is the service giving you by the each and every staff there, even in the peak time they always try to attend you individually still you complete the food. Best destination for family or group visit/party in quite and ambient place for fooding. In peak times there is little waiting is required but they attend you gracefully. Parking also available.

featured_reviews.name: Anish Karkera
featured_reviews.review_text:
We were just waiting to go here for a long time(years). And the experience was good. The garlic chilli pork ribs were awesome, pairs well with the sauces they give.
The chicken sui mai was a waste, don't order, it has no taste what so ever.
The Mongolian pork recommended by our server was top class delicious. We had it with the lings special fried rice that comes with chicken and shittake mushooms, this was also pretty damn good.
We were worried about the service being bad after looking at the reviews but everyone was super sweet to us, it's also important to note that we went on a Monday. Must be different on other days.
The prices are definitely on a higher end but the rice quantity was really good.
We're definitely going back this was totally worth it.

featured_reviews.name: A Ramadurai
featured_reviews.review_text:
The best Indo Chinese food in Mumbai in my opinion.

Last time we ate here was in 1993 and the bill was nearly Rs 3000 for 6 people

And now yesterday, we ate again to our hearts delight and the bill was Rs. 7555 for 4 people and this included alcohol too.

Hardly any price rise if you consider 3 decades difference.

The food was just superb.

Don't try to book table online, just turn up around 8pm and politely request the owner at the reception for a table and you get something very quickly.

featured_reviews.name: Shounak Nayak
featured_reviews.review_text: Hands down my favourite Chinese restaurant. The steamed wontons are absolutely unreal — easily the highlight every single time. The menu is insanely extensive, so one visit is never enough. Every time you go, there’s something new worth trying. Great food, great flavours, and the kind of place you keep coming back to.

featured_reviews.name: ivana edwards
featured_reviews.review_text:

My favs:

featured_reviews.name: Tarasangeeta Upadhyaya
featured_reviews.review_text: Nostalgia trip down memory lane- went there after almost 30 years! The place does not seem to have changed at all. Service is quick and good- our waiter neither wrote anything down, nor used a tablet and yet managed to remember everything!! Starters were fried corn curd- like a sweet corn soup but in solid form-wouldn’t order again, sesame chicken- surprisingly very good and the dim sum platter which they kindly made entirely in chicken. Two large chicken baos, two gyozas and two sui mai were enough for 4 people. The soup was shared by two people and was generously large. We should have stopped at this but greedily ordered chicken fried rice, noodles, Mongolian chicken ( like in a Manchurian sauce) and chilli chicken. All good. Doggie bags taken home!!

featured_reviews.name: SRP
featured_reviews.review_text:
First - if you are expecting Hakka (Indian style Chinese) dishes, you may be disappointed. These are close to real Chinese food - most dishes even if mentioned spicy they are not overly spicy as Hakka dishes.

Our first time trying the Vegan Corn Curd - almost like soft silken tofu consistency. The Spicy ones were really good. The Vegan Fried Wontons and Vegan Spinach were OK. The Spinach lacked sesame seeds/oil flavour. Wontons were a bit too much doughy and less filling.

After having so many starters/appetizers, not enough space for mains. The Vegan Buddha’s Delight was better. Lots of veggies and went well with steamed rice. The Vegan Steamed Buns were a good surprise for us as we don’t normally see this in India. Well made and went well the delight as well.

featured_reviews.name: Priyanka Thakur
featured_reviews.review_text:
I went to this restaurant with my friend. The place was empty on a Saturday evening, which should have been the first red flag. We ordered Veg kolhapuri, cheese naan and  Korean rice. The naan was undercooked and the dough was still raw inside. When the KOREAN RICE arrived it tasted like veg fried rice with Manchurian. Absolutely underwhelming. After 2 spoons I bite into something which almost broken off my teeth. It was a rock bigger than 1 cm. No exaggeration. I called over the waiter and showed him the rock. They offered to change the dish but how can you trust a place after they've served you food with big rock in it which almost broke my tooth. I don't know how did the chef not notice such a big rock while preparing the food, it's impossible to miss while cooking.
Oh and no regret/remorse/apology from the owner/cashier. Simply "Madam dish change kardu kya" from a waiter. How is this place still open. Is there no food inspection? They should be shut down.

featured_reviews.review_text:
A very good place for a family get together or just to grab some starters. The ambience is decent. The service is good, the food is delicious (can say that about the chinese.) If you happen to visit try their chicken fusion with prawns for starters, it's amazing.
It's priced moderately high.

featured_reviews.name: Anagha Nair
featured_reviews.review_text:
So we recently went to this restaurant in the evening.The resturant wasn't that busy and we could peacefully enjoy our food.

Sahibaan Oriental and Indian Resturant is a restaurant located in the heart of Colaba. It is a popular one for both locals and tourists.

The food is consistently good, with dishes that are flavorful. Portion sizes are generous, and the presentation is also appealing.

I would not recommend the sizzling Ice cream brownie from here,it was rather too hot and the brownie was not up to the mark.

The service staff were attentive and professional.
If you are looking for a special occasion restaurant in Mumbai, Then this is an good option.

Note:-As the serving portion of our spring roll was large we asked the waiter to pack it up,but forgot to pick it up when paying the bill.Please do not do this mistake as we did. If anyone wishes to parcel the food they didn't finish,remind them during bill payment.

Here is the list of food we ordered:-
Chicken Spring Roll
Chicken Lollipop
Pot Noodles
Sizzling Ice Cream Brownie

Overall, I would highly recommend The Sahibaan Oriental and Indian Resturant to anyone looking for a great dining experience in Colaba. It is a bit on the expensive side, but the quality of the food, service, and atmosphere is worth it.

Second time went there on 15 August 2024 suffered from severe food poisoning. Never going back here.

featured_reviews.review_text: One of the best places in Mumbai for Chinese food. Really good quality and their delicacies are amazing. Atmosphere is great too. Not too bright and some level of fencing between each table section to give you some comfort and separation from other guests. Service is great too. I love their chicken wings, it's spicy and tender.

featured_reviews.name: Ishita Mehta
featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited this restaurant during our outing to Marine Drive. The location is great if you’re around the area, but the overall experience was mixed.

One major issue was parking — it was quite difficult to find a spot nearby. There was also a long queue, so be prepared for a waiting time, especially during peak hours.

Coming to the food:

Foo Bao (Mushroom & Pepper) – 5/5 🌟
Definitely the best dish we tried. The flavors were on point and well balanced.

Shishito Charcoal Tempura Uramaki – 3/5
It was decent but nothing very memorable.

Pan-Fried Noodles – 1/5
This was disappointing and lacked flavor.

Overall, the food was average except for the Foo Bao, which really stood out.

Food: 3/5
Service: 3/5
Ambience: 3/5

Would visit again only for the Foo Bao.

featured_reviews.name: Sneha Chaturvedi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Went to Foo Town for dinner with my mum and had a great experience. The moment we walked in, the ambience stood out straight away! the lighting, decor, and overall atmosphere were beautiful and made the place feel really special.

The drinks were amazing as well, and the staff were all incredibly sweet and welcoming throughout the evening. The only issue we had was with one dish we ordered that never arrived. We asked about it twice and were told they would check on it, but it still didn’t come, so we ended up ordering another plate of sushi while we waited.

Thankfully, the missing dish wasn’t added to our bill, so no complaints there. It was a small hiccup, and I’d just suggest being a bit more mindful with orders, but apart from that everything was lovely.

The food we did receive was great, the atmosphere was stunning, and overall it was a really enjoyable dining experience.

featured_reviews.review_text:
The first thing to notice is comfortable booth seating, if you are lucky to get one of those spaces. Higher partitions provide good privacy between tables.

As expected, wide selection of drinks, including rice beer on tap.

Lotus stem bites were the only vegetarian option in our otherwise carnivore heavy selection...pork, tenderloin, prawns, crab meat, hamachi. Supremely satisfying.

Oh yes, and the famous blue rice - tenderly flavoured with a really quite special texture, easygoing on the palate, complimenting the rest of our food.

Wait staff tried pushing the Mount Foo-ji desert, but we opted for mango pudding and a hazelnut sweet instead.

There was a queue when we left after 10 pm, confirming the restaurant's popularity.

featured_reviews.name: Shweta Killedar
featured_reviews.review_text:
I was missing Thai food and found this place on Google. Honestly, everything here feels mid — food, service, ambience — definitely not worth the price. The flavors lacked authenticity and didn’t really satisfy the Thai food craving.

The papaya salad was good, tiger prawns were decent, and the cocktails were probably the best part of the meal.

Must try: Coconut pudding

Wouldn’t recommend ordering the charcoal chicken. The steamed John Dory had a distinct smell, though the taste itself was okish.

Overall, not a place I’d recommend if you’re looking for authentic Thai food.

featured_reviews.name: RD's Find
featured_reviews.review_text: Still the gold standard for Thai food in Mumbai. We had the John Dory in garlic sauce and the Thai Green Curry, and both were spectacular—perfectly balanced flavors that stay true to authentic Thai roots. The Tub Tim Grob (water chestnut dessert) was the perfect refreshing end to the meal. It’s expensive, but for the quality and the heritage, it’s worth every rupee.

featured_reviews.name: Buck Whas
featured_reviews.review_text: This is the most authentic Thai I’ve had in India. When I saw the menu and the dishes offered of which you don’t find in typical Thai restaurants I knew I had to check it out. The yum tua poo (wing bean salad) is a gem often overlooked but is amazing and if pescatarian do try it with prawn. I spoke with the head chef who has worked to maintain Thai flavors while respecting vegetarian majority. Nonetheless you request Thai style and she will turn it out authentic Thai style. I think this might be key if dining here and you have experience with Thai cuisine is that you need to specify that you wanted to be prepared a Thai style.

featured_reviews.name: Purvi Rathod
featured_reviews.review_text:
Everything from starters, mains and desserts was delicious. The team took extra care to make sure the food was non-spicy, as requested. Hard to pick one, but the desserts were delicious and very indulgent. It was my fist time tasting tub tim grob (water chestnuts in coconut milk with ice) and I loved it! We also ordered coconut pudding with sago and coconut ice cream and it was delicious too!

If you love thai food, I would highly recommend this place to you!

featured_reviews.name: Yogita N Goyal
featured_reviews.review_text: The food was authentic and very tasty. The bao Thai dish, similar to a dumpling, was soft and delicious. The Thai dessert Tub Tim Grob was too good and a perfect end to the meal. The staff was very courteous and had a great eye for detail. Service was smooth, and everything was done perfectly to make the atmosphere memorable for guests. Overall, a wonderful dining experience. It was much better experience than Taj Mahal Mumbai. Thanks to the staff.

featured_reviews.name: Neeraj Jain
featured_reviews.review_text: Great food and ambience! Right intent to serve but with questionable execution. We went on 13th April evening to celebrate a birthday and after the restaurant confirmed twice with us about the special occasion,  they neither offered any celebration nor even a greeting for the birthday! After we left, I called the hotel twice to give feedback and was told that the restaurant manager will call back but that did not happen either.That is not Taj hospitality standards that we are used to and hope it was just an aberration!

featured_reviews.name: Rishi Mistry
featured_reviews.review_text: After two weeks in India, we were ready for a little break from all of the wonderful Indian food we’ve had. Staying at the President Mumbai, we decided Thai Pavilion would be a convenient change of pace. I’m so glad we gave it a shot! All of our food was delicious - some of the tastiest Thai food I’ve had outside of Thailand. We shared the lotus and banana leaf salad, the red curry with shrimp, and the spicy basil rice. Everything was so delicious and satisfying. Our server was polite and attentive. The atmosphere is nice as well. Would love to return on our next trip to Mumbai!

featured_reviews.name: Sachi Gandhhi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Went to Thai pavilion for dinner recently and had a great experience! Loved the great service and delicious food.

They served pumpkin chips before the meal which were so light and crispy. I really enjoyed them.

For appetisers we had the pomelo salad which was my absolute favourite dish and I definitely recommend it. We also had the corn cakes which were good but could have had little more flavour. I ordered the Tom yum soup which was spicy and nice. We also got the lotus root chips which also tasted good with the house sauces that they provide.

For mains we had the pad Thai which I felt was a little bland and could have been more flavourful along with the water chestnut in a spicy sauce.

Although we liked some dishes more than others, they service was great and I will definitely be back for my favourites!

The ambience is beautiful, calm and very classy.
Perfect place for a relaxed and comfortable meal.
We started with Lychee & Jasmine Fizz and Sakura Cooler both were refreshing.
The Chicken Yakitori was smoky and juicy.
The Sui Mai dumplings were soft and flavourful.
The Dragon Roll sushi was honestly one of the best I’ve had.
The Truffle Udon noodles were comforting with a rich truffle taste.
The Prawn Thai curry with jasmine rice was my favourite dish.
We ended with a smooth and delicious Chinese mango pudding.
Special thanks to our steward Okchar he was very polite, helpful and made our dining experience even better.

featured_reviews.name: Mona Juneja

If you’re looking for Asian food in Colaba, Jia Oriental is a place worth visiting. The moment you step in, the ambience sets the tone... calm, modern, and elegant, making it ideal for a relaxed lunch or dinner.
We began with the Lychee & Jasmine Fizz, which was light, floral, and refreshing.
The Manchow soup that followed was comforting, flavourful, and well balanced.
One of my favourites from the meal was the pan-fried mushroom bao.. soft, juicy, and packed with umami flavours.
The Vegetable Dragon Roll, Signature Sushi, was equally enjoyable, with crispy vegetables and creamy avocado creating a nice balance of textures and taste.
The rice and noodles were simple and satisfying, complementing the rest of the dishes well.
A standout and something a little different was the Mushroom Chung Fung.. delicately steamed, silky in texture, and definitely a must-try if you enjoy subtle, comforting flavours.
We ended the meal with the Pull Me Up cake, which truly completed the experience. Rich, indulgent, and a perfect sweet finish.

Overall, Jia Oriental offers a lovely combination of good food, elegant ambience, and a relaxed dining experience. A great option in Colaba for anyone craving Asian flavours, sushi, and dim sums in a comfortable, well-designed setting.

featured_reviews.name: Roshani Batra
featured_reviews.review_text:
Kuai Kitchen- Its a cute little beautiful place right at the busy and famous shopping street, Colaba causeway. The bright interiors, vibrant lights, chinese and panda graffitis on the walls sum up the whole little place very warm and attractive. I was literally brightened up with the ambiance the moment I entered the place. As the name suggests, it is an Asian cuisine restaurant. The service is too quick and moreover, I found the staff very friendly and educated. I had a delish food eating experience there, and so far the place has topped my list for the Asian food in Mumbai. Dimsums were too good to go for. My friend had altogether amazing experience as she was busy drinking more glasses of 'Panda Passion' - their best mocktail made of ginger and lime soda.
Menu options- Dimsum, Appetizers, Sushi, Main course available in Veg, chicken and sea food (fish/prawn) options. Here's the details on what all I had my chopsticks on -
(1) Panda Passion- Their best signature drink to go for alongwith your asian meals.
(2) Wild mushroom Dumplings- The soft and tender mushroom dumplings were damn yummy.
(3) Spicy Chicken Dumplings- Being a non veggie, I just loved this spicy chicken dumplings served in mini dimsum basket.
(4) Veg Manchurian Bao - No words to define this one.
The best and delicious bao I ever had. This has crispy manchurian filling inside with healthy veggies in the bao which was tasting too yum.
(5) Fried Spring Roll- I didn't like this appetizer. I think why beacuse we indian normally have that taste of noodles filling inside the spring roll but this didnt had the noodles; I don't know what were the fillings.
(6) Kuai Special Mixed Vegetables Soy Chilly Garlic Sauce with Steamed Rice- It is an amazing combo where the sauce is extremely stocked up with different veggies, soy, chillies and goes well with the plain steam rice.
(7) Kuai Chocolate Panda- Its the best and unique dessert to go for. Steamed bao with chocolate ganache inside tastes yummy. What else do you look for in the dessert?
I had a wonderful experience dining there. You go colaba then make sure you do visit this place for eating scenes. I love asian food; they serve amazing chinese, japanese and thai cuisine dishes although limited options but definitely the tastiest ones. I would totally recommend this place; more than that I loved their food.

featured_reviews.name: rajesh jaiswar
featured_reviews.review_text:
A casual dining space, Kuai Kitchen is the newest offering from the Royal China stable, but you never would have guessed it. Its faux-grungy interiors, complete with graffiti-splattered walls and red-and-blue accents, are a far cry from the brand’s other restaurants, including the recently launched Jia, which caters to those with fat wallets. Moreover, it is matchbox-sized in comparison to its sprawling siblings. Kuai is the kind of place where you can make a mess and still breathe easy.

While the ambience is cheerful and the menu inviting, we dropped in to check if the wallet-friendly food matches up to the standard we’re used to expecting from the brand.
we’re surprised when we spot a sushi selection on Kuai’s menu. While the absence of sashimi and nigiri is sorely missed, we’re more than happy to dig into a Volcano Prawn Tempura Roll (Rs550), which comes drizzled with mayo ‘lava’. When it arrives (really quickly, may we add), the generous portion impresses us. Digging in, however, we realise that the chef may also have been a tad generous with the salt, a problem compounded by the fact that we’ve happily dunked our roll in soy sauce. That aside, we’re thoroughly content: the tempura prawns are juicy and crunchy, and the rice wrapping is not stodgy.

featured_reviews.name: dhawal gala
featured_reviews.review_text:
Stepping into Bayroute in Cuffe Parade is less like walking into a restaurant and more like embarking on an enchanting journey across the Mediterranean and Middle East. From the moment you cross the threshold, the attention to detail in the ambience, the authentic depth of the cuisine, and the seamless service work in perfect harmony to deliver an unforgettable fine-dining experience.

The Ambience: An Arabian Night's Dream
The ambience at Bayroute is truly its soul, beautifully capturing the old-world charm and opulence of the Levant. The decor is a magnificent blend of Moroccan, Turkish, and Arabian influences. Warm, rich lighting spills over intricately patterned floor tiles and tastefully adorned walls, which feature beautiful Turkish art. The seating is plush and comfortable, with Moroccan printed sofas that invite a leisurely, communal dining experience.

The entire space exudes a refined yet cozy atmosphere—perfect for a romantic evening, a sophisticated family dinner, or celebrating a special occasion. It’s an aesthetically curated masterpiece where every corner offers a visual delight, transporting you far away from the hustle of Mumbai.

The Food: An Authentic and Flavorful Expedition
The menu is an extensive map of culinary delights from countries like Egypt, Turkey, Lebanon, and Greece. It's a testament to authentic, well-researched cuisine, and every dish we tried was a revelation.The ingredients taste fresh, and the authentic spices are used with a delicate hand, ensuring the dishes are flavorful without being overwhelmingly heavy.

The Service: Courteous and Impeccable

A superb meal is only elevated by excellent service, and Bayroute truly shines here. The staff is exceptionally courteous, knowledgeable, and attentive. Our server was well-versed in the menu, offering insightful recommendations and patiently explaining the different regional nuances of the dishes. The pacing of the meal was perfect—neither rushed nor slow—allowing us to fully enjoy the experience. The attention to detail, from refreshing water glasses to clearing plates promptly, was seamless and professional.

Bayrute is more than just a restaurant; it’s a cultural experience. While it is on the higher end of the pricing scale, the unparalleled ambience, the authentic and delicious food, and the impeccable, friendly service make it absolutely worth the indulgence. It remains a must-visit destination for anyone looking to sample the finest Middle Eastern and Mediterranean cuisine in Mumbai in a truly magnificent setting.

featured_reviews.name: Monica
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re craving an authentic Middle Eastern experience in Mumbai, BAYROUTE is a place you simply can’t miss. We visited their Cuffe Parade outlet, and honestly, it felt like stepping straight into an Arabian dining room, warm, inviting, and rich in flavours.

Let’s start with their Classic Hummus, because that’s a non-negotiable order here. Creamy, smooth, and beautifully balanced, it’s topped with pine nuts, finished with labneh, and generously drizzled with good quality extra virgin olive oil. Simple, classic, and done perfectly, exactly how hummus should be.

For a refreshing sip, we tried their Reyhan, a soft beverage made with muddled orange and basil. Super refreshing, fragrant, and a great palate cleanser alongside the heavier dishes.

The Cheese Manakeesh was another standout. A soft Middle Eastern flatbread brushed with olive oil, loaded with lots of cheese. Comforting, indulgent, and perfect for sharing.

One of the highlights of the meal was the Dijaj Tria, a roasted trio of chicken kebabs featuring harissa spiced chicken, creamy shish taouk and Saffron Joojeh, served with garlic sauce, spicy schug and a punchy acili ezme dip. Every skewer brought something different to the table, and all of them were cooked beautifully.

Seafood lovers will enjoy the Butter Garlic Prawns, juicy, well-seasoned, and finished with rich garlic butter flavours without overpowering the prawns themselves.

We wrapped up with the Yemeni Mandi, which was aromatic, flavourful, and comforting, a wholesome dish that truly completes the Middle Eastern feast.

Overall, BAYROUTE delivers a genuine Arabian dining experience, from flavours to ambience. Perfect for anyone who enjoys Lebanese, Turkish, and Middle Eastern cuisine under one roof.
